alex (customer): Hey team — intermittent SSE disconnects from your /v1/stream endpoint. Client receives a few events then connection drops with no final event. Happens across browsers and node. Started after upgrade yesterday.

maya (Support): Sorry you're hitting this. Can you paste the initial request headers and any server response headers you see? Also which region and model?

alex (customer): Using EU region, model=open-llama-13b, Authorization: Bearer <redacted>. curl to repro: `curl -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \"https://eu.api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=open-llama-13b\"` — after ~10s we get no more events, client shows ECONNRESET in node. No 4xx in the client.

maya (Support): Thanks. Two quick possibilities: 1) a backend write error (EPIPE/EAGAIN) when client is slow -> server aborts, 2) auth/billing state that causes mid-stream termination (e.g., billing-bot forced close). Can you run with `-v` to show headers?

alex (customer): Added `-v`. Server initially responds `HTTP/1.1 200 OK`, `Content-Type: text/event-stream`, `x-request-id: r1234`, then stream stops. No 4xx/5xx. Logs attached (snippet):

sam (Eng SRE): Can you paste the client-side error trace? Also do you have any proxy/corp firewall? We had a CASE earlier where proxies buffered chunked responses and then closed after idle timeout -> partial output.

alex (customer): node stack: `Error: read ECONNRESET at TCP.onread (net.js:...)`. Browser console just reports EventSource connection closed. No corp proxy.

maya (Support): Ok. We'll try to reproduce from our side. In the meantime please try forcing smaller chunk flushes from our side by adding `?flush_interval_ms=50` to the request and see if behaviour changes. Also try connecting from a different network.

devon (Runtime): FYI I'm seeing similar errors in infra logs around that time: `write() returned -11 (EAGAIN) while sending to connection id=98765`, and shortly after `connection id=98765 aborted, cause=write_failed`. That pattern is classic slow consumer/backpressure where the kernel send buffer fills and our worker decides to abort to protect resources.

sam (Eng SRE): We also have a few entries showing `client-ip=22.33.44.55 keepalive_timeout=60s write_bytes=0` then `socket closed by peer` — means client likely stopped reading.

alex (customer): Interesting. Could that be related to auth expiration? Token was valid the whole time. Also billing status is OK.

billing-bot: Notice: account acct_9 flagged transiently for over-usage at 2026-02-10T14:22:10Z — automated rate throttle applied for 30s window.

maya (Support): Aha — the billing-bot event could explain abrupt mid-stream termination if the control-plane signalled a throttle and our worker closed the SSE channel rather than sending a final event. We'll check logs for the request x-request-id (r1234).

devon (Runtime): Confirmed in infra: r1234 had throttle signal at 14:22:10Z. Worker logs:```
worker[pid=1423] INFO handle_stream r1234 start
worker[pid=1423] WARN send_event write() returned -11 EAGAIN
worker[pid=1423] INFO throttle applied for account acct_9
worker[pid=1423] ERROR abort_stream reason=quota_throttle
```

sam (Eng SRE): That sequence is not ideal — we should emit an SSE event like `event: throttle
data: {"reason":"quota","retry_after":30}

` before closing, instead of abrupt CLOSE. For now, workaround on client: implement EventSource `onerror` to automatically attempt reconnect with exponential backoff and re-auth.

alex (customer): Can you confirm whether the server will send a 402 or a throttle event in next patch? Abrupt close is hard to detect reliably on the client.

maya (Support): Engineering is going to push a fix: 1) when control-plane requests throttle/close we will attempt to send a final SSE error event (text/event-stream) and flush before closing, 2) improve backpressure handling: increase per-connection sndbuf and switch to non-blocking retry loop with small backoff rather than immediate abort.

devon (Runtime): Implementation notes for the fix: - call res.write(`event: error
data: {"code":"quota_throttle","retry":30}

`) then flush and wait up to 500ms for socket to drain, if still blocked -> close with reason header. Also add metric `sse.abort_due_to_eagain`.

sam (Eng SRE): Repro steps we used:
1) Start a client that reads very slowly (`while(true){ await sleep(2000); read() }`)
2) Hit /v1/stream with a token that gets rate-limited mid-stream (we simulate via billing API toggle)
3) Observe worker logs show EAGAIN then abort, client sees ECONNRESET.

maya (Support): Alex — can you try the temporary workarounds: a) set flush_interval_ms=50, b) add EventSource `onerror` that reconnects and resends any partial prompt state, c) use a non-buffering proxy (nginx without proxy_buffering on) if you have a gateway. Let us know results.

alex (customer): Will try now. Also can you add logging for x-request-id in your abort messages so we can correlate if it happens again?

devon (Runtime): Done — we will include x-request-id in the abort trace and add a user-visible header `x-sse-abort-reason` on the connection close event for easier triage.

maya (Support): Follow-up: we'll schedule a canary patch tomorrow to send final SSE error events on throttle and to reduce aggressive aborts during transient backpressure. I'll update this thread when deployed. :thumbsup: 

alex (customer): Thanks — appreciated. I'll report back after testing the workaround.

sam (Eng SRE): If the customer still sees abrupt closes after the patch, we'll escalate to runtime team and capture tcpdump for the session.

maya (Support): Closing loop for now; keeping thread open until customer confirms.
